subject: Azure Marketplace private offer — commitment vs flat-fee packaging and channel split
messages:
From: Alex Kelley <alex.kelley@cloudbroker.io>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>, procurement@graybox.ai
Date: 2028-03-14 09:12 PDT
Subject: Azure private offer packaging question — commitment vs flat fee and channel passback

Hi Michael and team,

Quick question from GrayBox procurement — they are evaluating two packaging paths for the Azure private offer: a 12-month usage commitment (metered, with monthly true-up) vs a single flat monthly list-price SKU (simpler billing). The customer wants to understand how each option impacts: 1) effective unit economics after the Azure marketplace fee, 2) the reseller passback to CloudBroker (their channel partner), and 3) our ability to offer mid-term tier bumps without a full contract amendment.

Details: expected first-year consumption is ~2.1M tokens/month (~2.5M with growth), baseline list price is $0.0009/token. GrayBox asked for a 30% list discount to get to a committed-rate equivalent — but they want to keep the reseller margin at ~18% net to CloudBroker.

Can you confirm what packaging you recommend and a sample waterfall (list price -> marketplace fee -> reseller passback -> net to Redwood for both commitment and flat SKU)? Also attach any sample PO language for mid-term tier increases.

Thanks,
Alex (on behalf of GrayBox procurement)

---
Attachment: GB_AI_Azure_PO_draft_v1.pdf (PDF stub)

From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Kelley <alex.kelley@cloudbroker.io>, procurement@graybox.ai
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-03-14 10:02 PDT
Subject: Re: Azure private offer packaging question — commitment vs flat fee and channel passback

Alex — thanks for the detailed note. Looping in Ben and Irene to confirm economics and channel plumbing. High level upfront: both options are viable but have different operational and pricing trade-offs. I sketched a short comparison below and attached a waterfall spreadsheet.

Summary (quick):
- Commitment (metered with monthly true-up): better for unit price predictability and easiest for providing deeper discounts tied to committed volume; supports mid-term increases via agreed uplift clauses (recommended language attached). Slightly more complex billing but lower per-token net.
- Flat monthly SKU (list-fee): simplest for procurement and invoicing, easier for GrayBox to forecast costs month-to-month. Less flexible for mid-term growth without amendment; to preserve channel margin you usually need a higher list price or a surcharge mechanism.

Proposed sample waterfall (approx):
1) List price: $0.0009/token
2) Azure marketplace fee: 8% (marketplace take — may vary by program) -> $0.000828/token
3) Reseller passback (CloudBroker target 18% of list): -$0.000162/token (18% of list)
4) Net to Redwood before discounts/credits: $0.000666/token

If we instead offer a 30% list discount to the customer (committed-rate equivalent), the numbers look like: 
- Discounted customer price: $0.00063/token (30% off list)
- Marketplace fee still applies on list or on transaction? Ideally applied on list; if applied on net sale, marketplace will reduce take — we need to lock on that in the PO.
- Reseller passback at 18% of list remains $0.000162/token -> net to Redwood ~ $0.000468/token.

Ben/Irene — can you validate the marketplace fee assumption and whether reseller passbacks should be calculated on list vs net in our recommended PO language? Also attaching a recommended clause for mid-term tier increases that preserves channel passback percentage.

Next steps: Ben to confirm the channel math, Irene to propose PO clause. Michael

--
Michael Grant
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
Attachment: margin-waterfall-v2.xlsx (XLSX stub)

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-03-14 13:28 PDT
Subject: Re: Azure private offer packaging question — commitment vs flat fee and channel passback

All — validated the quick numbers. A few operational notes and an exact waterfall for procurement: 

Assumptions I used:
- Azure marketplace fee: 8% of the transaction (standard in their private offer program today)
- Reseller passback target: 18% of list price (as requested) -> this is typically computed on invoice list amount to keep the channel economics stable regardless of customer discounts.
- Committed discount: provided as discount off list in the private offer metadata (so customer sees discounted SKU).

Waterfall — Commitment (metered, 12m):
- List price: $0.0009/token
- Marketplace fee (8% of transaction): $0.000072/token -> paid to Azure
- Reseller passback (18% of list): $0.000162/token -> paid to CloudBroker via our channel process (we pass through in settlement)
- Committed discount to customer (30% off list): customer billed $0.00063/token
- Net to Redwood: list - marketplace fee - reseller passback - discount impact = $0.0009 - 0.000072 - 0.000162 - 0.00027 = $0.000396/token (note: because discount is applied to customer invoice, the marketplace fee calculation can change depending on whether Azure charges on list or net — need to confirm)

Waterfall — Flat monthly SKU (single monthly invoice):
- List price set higher to preserve channel margin after flat discounting (example: set list to $0.00105/token then give 20% off for pricing parity)
- Marketplace fee at 8% (higher absolute $ because list is higher)
- Reseller passback still anchored to list to keep CloudBroker at 18% -> operationally simpler for channel but results in slightly higher gross $ to Azure and passback.

Operational recommendations: 
1) For GrayBox we recommend the Commitment path. It gives us levers for aggressive unit pricing while keeping channel economics stable.
2) In the PO, require marketplace fees and reseller passback be computed on list price (not net after discount) — this protects the channel and simplifies our settlement.
3) Include a mid-term tier uplift clause: allow GrayBox to increase committed months or tokens at pre-agreed bucketed pricing steps, and preserve the reseller % on incremental volume. We propose a simple tranche table (attached) and an auto-notice window (30 days).

I'll prepare a short snippet to drop into the PO and loop legal if needed.

Ben
Sr Manager, Pricing Operations

---
Quoted formula and example figures attached in margin-waterfall-v2.xlsx

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-03-14 15:03 PDT
Subject: Re: Azure private offer packaging question — commitment vs flat fee and channel passback

Michael/Ben — added legal-friendly PO language below. This text assumes Azure computes marketplace fees on the invoice line item (list minus any marketplace discounts). If Azure insists on using net invoice amounts, the marketplace take will be slightly lower and we should adjust the reseller passback calculation accordingly. Recommend we push to have passback anchored to list.

Suggested PO clause (drop-in):
"""
1) Pricing and Marketplace Fees: The Parties agree that list prices for Marketplace Private Offer SKUs will be as detailed in Schedule A. Marketplace fees charged by the Marketplace Provider (e.g., Azure) shall be applied per Marketplace Provider policy. For clarity, reseller passback percentages described in Section 2 shall be calculated on the SKU list price regardless of any customer-specific discounts applied in the Private Offer metadata.

2) Reseller Passback: Redwood will pay CloudBroker a reseller passback equal to 18% of the SKU list price on each transaction covered by this Private Offer. Passback payments will be settled monthly via Redwood's channel settlement process.

3) Mid-Term Volume Increases: Customer may request increases to committed volumes. Such increases executed within the term will be priced according to the tranche table in Schedule B and shall preserve the reseller passback percentage on incremental volumes. Changes that materially affect annual committed spend must be documented via an addendum with a 30-day effective notice unless both Parties agree otherwise.

4) Marketplace Fee Treatment: If Marketplace Provider calculates fees on the net transaction amount rather than list, the Parties will reconcile the impact during the first billing cycle and make a one-time equitable adjustment to passback payments to preserve pre-agreed reseller economics.
"""

If legal signs off, this should be fine for procurement. I also added a 30-day auto-notice for tier bumps so we can execute faster.

Irene
Head of Partner Contracts
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Azure private offer packaging question — commitment vs flat fee and channel passback

Alex / GrayBox team — thanks for the patience. Ben and Irene validated the economics and attached PO language. Short answers: we recommend the 12-month metered commitment for the reasons outlined (lower net unit cost, straightforward tranche upgrades, preserves CloudBroker margin). Key asks from our side to finalize the private offer: 

1) Confirm whether Azure will accept reseller passback as 18% of list in the private offer (we'll push to capture that in the private offer metadata and settlement schedule).
2) Confirm expected monthly token profile (you sent ~2.1M/month — please provide a month-by-month expected burn if possible for the first 6 months).
3) Sign and return the attached PO; we can finalize private offer metadata and provisioning within 7 business days after PO execution.

If GrayBox prefers the flat SKU route we can provide a sample list price that achieves approximate parity but it will involve slightly different settlement mechanics. Happy to jump on a 20-minute call if helpful.

Next steps: Alex to confirm Azure passback acceptance and share month-by-month consumption; we'll pull legal for a quick review once you accept the PO language.

Thanks,
Michael
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
